checks: At a proper normalized cut, the first variation makes F_x differentiable and threshold stationarity gives F_x′(1)=dP. The bounded projection density and E[G⁻¹]=1/d give f_V(0)=P. If exactly one margin c_p is positive, the other nonzero phases give Y>0 almost surely. The conditional density at z is c_p⁻¹exp(−(z+Y)/c_p) on z+Y>0 and zero on z+Y<0. It is bounded by c_p⁻¹ and continuous at zero for almost every Y, yielding f_V(0)=P/c_p. Strict row positivity excludes c_p=1. Zero margins do not enter this argument.

Log-concavity implies f(z)≤P exp(ℓz) for z≥0 with ℓ=f′(0)/P. If ℓ<−1, its integral is less than P. If ℓ=−1, equality of integrals and continuity force equality pointwise. Since 0<c_j<1 at each positive margin, a λ>1 with λc_j<1 for every j gives a finite product moment, contradicting the rate-one positive tail. Thus f′(0)>−P.

P(c+s1)=Pr(c·U≥−s) gives its second shift derivative −f_{c·U}′(0). Joint C² makes the projection density C¹ near zero. In the gamma difference quotient the small-G part is bounded by a constant times |z|⁻¹ times the integral of G^(d−1) up to |z|/δ, hence O(|z|^(d−1)); the rest is dominated by G⁻². The exact gamma moment is Γ(d−1)/Γ(d+1)=1/[d(d−1)] and remains finite for d=2. These signs give the stated B and its strict positivity.

Differentiating the row gradient tP^(−1/d−1)g/d at t=1 gives L_xt=K(η−dg), since 1ᵀg=dP. The row-row block is K[(d+1)ggᵀ/(dP)−H], and direct threshold differentiation gives L_tt=K[d(d−1)P−1ᵀH1]. The actual nearby minimizers are proper and converge by the unique-threshold lemma, so the C¹ implicit critical branch is the minimizer. Differentiation of the envelope gradient gives the stated Schur complement.

Let A=η·v for g·v=0. Before the rank-one subtraction, the divided-by-K quadratic on v+s1 is −vᵀHv−2sA+s²(2dP+B). The subtracted square is [A−s(dP+B)]²/B. Expanding leaves −vᵀHv−(A−sdP)²/B, and v=0,s=1 gives −Kd²P²/B<0.
